name: social-flow
description: Channel-based short-form and long-form content pipeline. Pick the format when you start a storyboard — 9:16 shorts for Threads, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, or 16:9 YouTube long-form with chapters — then author the storyboard under data/[channel]/episodes/[topic]/, produce the video and the per-platform text, and publish it after a HITL approval gate. Long-form episodes mix clips you film yourself with generated scenes, and scenes that need words or diagrams on screen become HTML slides — planned in the storyboard, authored only after approval; a slide that states a value becomes a motion slide (count-ups, growing bars, steps entering on their sentence), rendered locally frame by frame at no cost and admitted to the build after the contract checker and the author's own read of its key frames. A beat that shows something happening can instead become a footage slide — one generated clip per narration sentence inside the HTML slide, with a wordless mark (a route, an arrow, a ring, hatching) drawn on over the picture, so a two-minute short can run fifty shots. Narration defaults to your own voice on every scene, so the shooting script carries the lines for every shot: filmed shots get screen, action, lines and a filename, the rest are voice-only recordings. Research writes three scenario candidates in one fixed shape — the thought to leave the viewer with, a dramatised hook, what actually happened, what it means now, two or three present-day cases, a question to the viewer, and a CTA — and shows all three in full for you to pick. The narration is then written before any shot and read on its own twice, in order, with the sentences handed to the reviewer inline — once for whether they alone carry the episode, once for whether the words are what a person says — each looped to 95 in at most three reads. The board itself gets the contract checkers and the author's own read: the six board reads, the plan review and the slide loop of earlier versions were measured at more than half of an episode's tokens and are no longer called, and anything the author leaves unresolved goes onto the approval screen. The autoproduce skill runs the same path unattended, replacing the approval gate with the machine gates and an economy tier. Per-platform setup and growth skills open the accounts and then run autonomous growth loops. A built-in MCP server ships 61 tools (52 without credentials) — publishing, insights, search, open data, and image, video, voice and music generation — with no external MCP dependency.
